content:
Nina G.: FYI I'm prototyping a response-shim that normalizes old v1 response envelopes to the new v2 shape at the edge. clients still expecting the old keys won't break during migration.
Omar H.: top-level question: do we transform at ingress or at the service boundary (sidecar)?
Nina G.: ingress plugin (nginx + lua) so we avoid touching app code. lighter ops surface and easier to flip.
Li W.: how are we handling streaming responses? v2 introduced chunked JSON-stream with `event` frames; v1 expected a single JSON object.
Nina G.: shim will detect streaming by `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and coalesce into a single object up to a 10s window or 1MB cap, then emit the legacy envelope. For long streams we return a 503 with a `Retry-After` and a friendly error telling clients to upgrade.
Tanya (SRE): watch out for memory pressure if we coalesce many concurrent streams. what's the expected mem per request?
Nina G.: cap per coalesced request at 1MB; we also limit concurrent coalesces per worker to 16. fallback policy is immediate 503 once we hit the limit.
Omar H.: perf numbers?
Nina G.: microbenchmarks: coalesce median overhead 2.4ms p50, p95 18ms for 700KB responses. Single-object transforms are 0.7ms median.
Li W.: client compatibility: do we add headers to signal we mutated the response? useful for telemetry and debugging.
Nina G.: yes `X-Redwood-Response-Shim: coalescer-v1`, and `X-Redwood-Response-Mode: legacy` when we downgrade a stream to object.
Tanya (SRE): telemetry/alerts: add `shim.coalesce.drop_rate` and `shim.coalesce.mem_limit_hits`. Alert if drop_rate > 0.5% over 10m or mem_limit_hits > 5/min.
Nina G.: will add. infra-bot: [automated] Dashboard created: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/resp-shim/resp-shim-coalesce showing shim.coalesce.latency, shim.coalesce.drop_rate, req.duration, worker.rss.
Omar H.: what about cache semantics? v2 streaming responses rely on progressive tokens; legacy cache expects whole-body keys. If we coalesce we'll increase cacheability but could hide streaming regressions.
Li W.: prefer to preserve canonical request fingerprint. If we downgrade, generate synthetic cache key that includes `shim_mode=coalesced` so caches are distinct.
Nina G.: implemented plan: `sha256(route||normalized_response||shim_mode)` and a flag in cache metrics to separate coalesced hits.
Tanya (SRE): rollout plan & kill-switch?
Nina G.: feature-flagged per-tenant, default off. Canary 10 tenants, then ramp. Kill switch is a one-click global toggle in ingress admin that returns `418 I'm a teapot` (so we spot it immediately) and sets `Retry-After: 30`.
Omar H.: deprecation policy: how long do we keep the shim?
Nina G.: recommend 120 days from GA announcement. We'll publish telemetry showing remaining v1 clients daily.
Li W.: testing: unit parser tests, stream-coalesce fuzzing, integration with older SDKs and e2e with SDK compat-mode header. Also run a soak for 48h under production-like traffic.
Nina G.: security: we use a strict JSON streamer checker; reject non-utf8 payloads and untrusted binary frames. Rejections increment `shim.coalesce.rejected_malformed`.
Tanya (SRE): runbook: have an `shim.emergency_quarantine` step that rotates ingress workers and sets the toggle. Add postmortem checklist if any canary errors exceed 0.1% error rate.
Omar H.: docs: add a short how-it-works note in the compat playbook and an example curl showing both modes.
Nina G.: example curl: `curl -H "Accept: application/legacy+json" https://canary.ingress.api/v2/stream` (shim will coalesce into legacy envelope).
Li W.: fallback for critical tenants: support-mode allows us to proxy to a compatibility backend that runs a dedicated transformer. But require manual approval and audit trail.
Tanya (SRE): add guardrails: support-mode limited to 3 tenants and auto-expire after 14 days.
infra-bot: [automated] Deployed `resp-shim:staging/coalesce` to canary cluster at 2026-04-02T09:12:00Z
deploy-bot: [staging] deployment started for `resp-shim:staging/coalesce`
Nina G.: I'll post canary metrics in #eng-infra 1h after deploy. Please review dashboard and voice any aborts.
Omar H.: thanks. if canary looks good we can try a 20% env rollout and keep an eye on p99 latency deltas.
Li W.: +1. schedule 30min post-canary review.
Tanya (SRE): and run the memory-pressure load test: 50 concurrent coalesces with 900KB streams for 15m. abort criteria: worker.rss > 2GB or mem_limit_hits > 50.
Nina G.: noted; will attach the test script and results.
